text:
Josh Morrissey missed about a month with an upper-body injury, left a game against Colorado on Oct. 7 after less than ten minutes, and returned against New Jersey on Nov. 10. Winnipeg hasn't eased him in: he played 32.8 minutes in a 5-4 win over Chicago, part of a run of three straight wins since his return.

Seven games is too small a sample to judge, so treat these numbers lightly. He has 5 assists and no goals, his scoring rate of 1.86 points per 60 minutes sits inside our range for him, and Winnipeg has scored 6.4 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. That on-ice luck won't last, but it also isn't the story yet.

The bigger picture comes from last season. Evolving-Hockey had him 17th of 215 defensemen at 2.5 wins above replacement, mostly from even-strength offense. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 61% of his exits leaving the zone with possession and 6.0 primary shot assists per 60, 86th percentile among defensemen. That is a defenseman who moves the puck forward cleanly. Watch for his first goal and where his minutes settle.
headline: Morrissey is back and the minutes came with him
